frontier.hypothesis: The loop.c:1631 LICM decision on the 0x91A2B3C5 (/1800) magic is the entire remaining 16 points, and under the shipped compiler configuration it needs a loop-2 RTL insn_count of at least 123 that no measured spelling approaches.
frontier.mechanism: loop.c:1631 moves the constant-load movable iff threshold * savings * m->lifetime >= insn_count; threshold is 122 (loop.c:532, no call in the loop), savings is 1 (loop.c:897, hard-coded for a move_insn) and lifetime is 1 (loop.c:791), so the product is pinned at 122 and only insn_count is C-movable. The five loop-2 spellings measured across s1/s2/s3 give insn_counts of 44, 55, 55, 62 and 62, and s2 measured the gate flipping between 120 and 123.
frontier.next_probe: Do NOT re-derive the gate (s2 FACT 8 measured the 120/123 boundary) and do NOT re-derive the -msoft-float story (s3 FACT 19 supersedes s2 FACT 11: the flag alone leaves this body at 16). The one untried honest direction is a rederive-modality session looking for a different decomposition of the three clock fields (minutes / seconds / hundredths) that is byte-equivalent to the current loop but carries more pre-combine RTL. If that comes back empty, the residual is compiler-configuration-bound and the disposition question belongs to a later escalation-modality session, not to a structural one.

frontier.hypothesis: The 16-point body's two constructs - the split accumulators (flags/flags0/flags1/flags2) and the `i = 0;` hoist - need an admissibility ruling before any submission, and respelling them to dodge that is the wrong move.
frontier.mechanism: Neither construct is dead and neither is a coercion: every split local is written once and holds a value that IS stored to p[8] and read by the next arm, and `i = 0;` is the loop's real initialisation. But flags0 and flags1 are each read TWICE (the store and the next arm), so this is not the once-written/once-read named-intermediate shape in .claude/rules/narrow-byte-args-packed-call.md, and the only reason not to reuse one `v` is codegen - which is the shape the frozen list covers under 'variable reuse for codegen control' read in reverse.
frontier.next_probe: Nothing to submit while the body is at 16. When a future session reaches distance 0 from this chassis, file a ruling-request naming BOTH constructs and quoting the candidate.c admissibility note, rather than a speculative candidate-ready. The fallbacks if either is refused are the split-only body at 18 (tmp/grind/func_80035280/s3/v/v4.c) and the un-split body at 39 (rejected/s3-single-accumulator-global-allocno-score39.c).

frontier.hypothesis: The reg_n_deaths == 1 lever found here is generic and should transfer to other queue functions whose target holds an accumulator in $v0/$v1 across a straight-line block where our build puts it in an argument register.
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc.c:472's eligibility test is not specific to this function: any pseudo written more than once in a block is refused local allocation and gets whatever global-alloc has left after the short single-death temps have taken $v0/$v1/$a0. Splitting the multi-written variable into one local per value restores local eligibility and the qty_compare priority ordering.
frontier.next_probe: Cheap and mechanical: for any function stuck on an argument-register accumulator, grep its .lreg slice for a pseudo that 'dies in N places' with N > 1 and cross-check the ';; N regs to allocate' list in .greg. If the accumulator is in the global list, try the one-local-per-value split. Worth a cross-function sweep by a solver-modality or forensics session; it is not a func_80035280-specific finding.
